set.body:
Outcome: make new branch scores depend on geometry at declared scales rather than the number of sampled points.

Scope: R/mat.R and narrowly required kernels/tests. Preserve mlv2023 behavior. Define new mirror/straightness scoring using geometric residuals or curvature with explicit scale and endpoint rules; do not retain (1-1/n)^power as a geometric score. Integrate and smooth parallelism/taper over arc length. Specify dimensionless derivative combinations and all reference lengths rather than relabeling pixel/sample formulas. Separation requires an explicit reference radius r0 in the same unit as R, a defined valid domain, and a versioned formula (candidate 1-r0/R).

Acceptance:
- Pass frozen constant-radius, straight, curved, and tapered witnesses across sample densities and physical calibrations.
- A perfectly straight branch has the declared ideal new-method score irrespective of n; short or degenerate support has explicit validity behavior.
- Verify dimensional scaling, derivative estimates against independent formulas, boundary behavior, and smoothing/exponent effects.
- Preserve NA versus valid zero and surface the support/mapping coverage needed to interpret summaries.
- Document that an axis-straightness proxy does not establish global reflection symmetry.
- Legacy default outputs still satisfy existing numeric parity fixtures, including documented port corrections.

Dependency rationale: reuse the reviewed arc-length representation, physical-scale conventions, and curvature primitives from mlv-curvature-estimators for branch integration and the chosen straightness estimator. Keep one writer per shared numerical scope.
set.title: Implement physical-scale branch scores independent of sample count
